html:
The Snoqualmie are a Coast Salish people of the Snoqualmie River valley, in the foothills of the Cascades east of Seattle. Their language is Lushootseed, shared with the Duwamish and other Puget Sound peoples.

They fished salmon, hunted elk and deer in the mountains and traded across the passes. Snoqualmie Falls is a sacred place for them. Their leader Patkanim signed the Treaty of Point Elliott in 1855, which gave most of their land to the United States in exchange for reserves and fishing rights. The Snoqualmie were long left without a reservation of their own; the tribe won federal recognition in 1999.
